title: Round 13 Post-Qualifying Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following qualifying here in Qatar. Joining us in P3 from Rodin Motorsport, it's Alexander Dunne. In second place from MP Motorsport, it's Gabriele Minì and from Van Amersfoort Racing capturing his first pole position in Formula 2, it's the reigning F3 champion, Ugo Ugochukwu. Ugo, congratulations. First F2 pole, how does that feel?

Ugo Ugochukwu: Feels pretty amazing to be on pole on debut. Yeah, it's a dream start really to Formula 2. It's been a really good day overall. I was feeling really good with the car from lap one in Practice, which is really important, starting in a front foot. And then yeah, I just made the right steps throughout Practice, throughout Qualifying to really get me in a good position towards the end of the session and yeah, managed to put it all together. So yeah, really happy with how the day unfolded.

FIA Formula 2: Just take me through that final push lap.

Ugochukwu: Yeah, it was a nice lap. It was straight onto an out lap and then a push lap. So everyone was really struggling to get the tyres in the right window in these cold conditions. So sector one was definitely very tricky. And then, you know, the tyre came alive throughout the lap and I just could push more and more and more and then sector three really gave it everything.

FIA Formula 2: What was your personal expectation coming into this weekend? I mean, because this really does seem like a dream scenario for yourself.

Ugochukwu: Yeah, definitely. I think, you know, I expected to be fighting for the front. I expected to be competitive, but to be on pole is super, super nice. I think after Practice, you know, is when I really felt, you know, the potential was there to be in the top three after, you know, getting a feel of how we were pace wise and yeah, and the Qualifying. I was just confident to go out and put it all together.

FIA Formula 2: Well, congratulations on the pole, Ugo. Gabriele, coming to you. Congrats on the P2. Did the track feel like it was coming more towards you as the session was moving on and the temperatures were starting to come down?

Gabriele Minì: Yeah, I mean, in general, it was a good session, but I think it was a bit the same for everyone. Of course, cooler condition, you know, a bit better, you know, what the track conditions are like, less fuel. So, of course, everything all together, you know, makes you go faster, of course. But in the end, yeah, we struggled a bit more in the first run. We did a small change, you know, during the break, and then we managed to do a decent lap at the end, which was good enough for the front row.

FIA Formula 2: You're locked in this championship battle between Nikola and Alex. What was your mindset coming into this one?

Minì: To be honest, I mean, realistically, I'm a bit more, you know, further away from them, so I need two very, very good weekends for me to catch them, and they need to do a, let's say, a not-so-good one. So, realistically, my main focus was to gain back the qualifying form that we had at the beginning of the year, which we did so far. Usually, the races have been a bit stronger, you know, comparing to qualifying, so hopefully it will be again the case this weekend, so we can fight for good points.

FIA Formula 2: It's a tough track to pass on. Where do you think there could be some opportunities for yourself on Sunday?

Minì: In the corners? Yeah. And at the start, probably. I mean, you know, I'm pretty sure that everyone will be straight on point already for tomorrow's starts, but, you know, we'll try to use the inexperience that Ugo has yet, even though he showed that, you know, he's straight away fast to try and, you know, lead the pack on Sunday. But, first of all, we have to try and gain good points, as usual, on the sprint without getting any stupid penalties or getting involved in a crash, and then we have to try and maximise Sunday.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on the P2, Gabriele. Alex, coming to you, congrats on the P3. That looked like a good lap. Can you take me through it?

Alexander Dunne: It wasn't a very good one, to be honest. No, I mean, it was actually, it was a very good lap until Sector 3, and then in Sector 3, I made two pretty big mistakes where I lost quite a lot of time. But I think, in general, I really struggled to kind of get comfortable with the car and find the balance. I think I felt like we were reasonably out of, I think, the window of how I, I think the car in general has had good performance, but I think in terms of how I like the car to feel, we were quite a bit far out of the window at the beginning of FP, and I think we've slowly kind of chipped away at it. You know, we made some pretty reasonable changes before Quali, and then we made another fairly big step during Quali as well. And so for that final push lap, thankfully, when it mattered, it kind of came all together and the pace was strong again. So yeah, it was definitely a lot more difficult than it needed to be, and probably the most under pressure we've been going into that final run.

FIA Formula 2: But you managed to put it together, and P3 is still a good place to be. Same question for you that I'd put to Gabriele, but you're in this championship battle with Nikola. What's the mindset coming into qualifying here tonight?

Dunne: I mean, to be honest, like two or three weekends ago, I had pretty much written myself off from the championship. I think I was like 60 points off the lead or something, and now we're right in it, which, you know, I couldn't really believe after Baku, to be honest. But I think one thing that's allowed us to get back into the championship fight is by not worrying about it. You know, I think I just told myself that if we can continue to have good Qualifying pace and try and fix our race pace a little bit and get the most out of every weekend until the end of the year, then something good might come, and it might not.

FIA Formula 2: So I think that attitude has kind of gotten you back in the fight, and it would be the wrong idea now to shift your mindset to suddenly focus on the championship. With that being said, taking a look at Sunday, what do you think is possible from P3?

Dunne: Well, I think a good result is definitely possible. You know, Gabriele's been very quick in the races this year. Ugo has clearly showed he's really strong, but I guess his race pace is more of a bit of an unknown as he hasn't raced in this championship yet. So I guess that could be something that we could take advantage of, but I'm sure he'll be on it. So, you know, we'll have to wait and see, but we're in a good place to try and move forward, and if we don't, then that's fine as well. You know, I just want to bring home good points.

title: Tsolov aiming to fightback in the races after ‘tricky’ Qualifying in Lusail
excerpt:
Nikola Tsolov is aiming to fight back in both races after a mixed Qualifying result

Nikola Tsolov is looking to move forward in both Lusail races, as he reflected on a tricky Qualifying session and the potential for a three-way fight for the title.

The Campos Racing driver finished seventh but was left to rue mistakes that took away a potential place in the top three.

But Tsolov was not too down beat as he explained how it was all part of a new approach he adopted in the hopes of qualifying in a higher position.

“It was a bit of a tricky one,” said Tsolov. “It was more messy than usual in Qatar. But just a bit of a messy one for me generally.

“On set one I made a mistake, and then on set two on my best lap again, I did a mistake and I was coming for a P3. Nothing like pole, but it's not great. I over-pushed a little bit in the last sector and then that cost me the lap.

Tsolov qualified seventh in the Lusail Qualifying session

“But that was the approach I was aiming for this weekend, to loosen up, push a bit more and try to see what happens instead of just putting a clean lap together. But that's the result this time.

“I have one more opportunity next week. For now, we focus on the races which are going to be completely different to the quali.”

Round 13 Post-Qualifying Press Conference

QUALIFYING: Ugochukwu takes stunning debut pole position in Lusail

Looking ahead to both the Sprint and Feature Race, Tsolov is hopeful that he can move forward and score some big points.

“If the track allows overtaking, I think I can move forward because generally in the races I have more pace,” said Tsolov.

“We’ll have to wait and see. Overtaking is difficult here, so I’m hoping things go my way.”

Tsolov is looking to fight back in the races in what he thinks is now a three-way title fight

Tsolov is starting behind title rivals Gabriele Minì and Alexander Dunne – who are second and third – but even with Rafael Câmara’s promotion to Formula 1, it does not change much for the Bulgarian.

“It doesn’t change much,” said Tsolov on Câmara not being around for the final two rounds. “I think I still do the same job every weekend, and in the end, he's gone.

“But I still have Alex and Minì, so I think it's going to be a three-way fight. Minì seems to have found pace again, so it will be cool.”

title: Inthraphuvasak handed grid penalty for Lusail races
excerpt:
ART Grand Prix's Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak has been handed a grid penalty following Practice in Lusail.

The Thai driver was alleged to have made a yellow flag infringement during the session.

Afterwards, the Stewards reviewed video, GPS data, telemetry and video evidence and heard from both driver and ART team representative. They determined Car 17 failed to respect yellow flag requirements at Turn 11, constituting a breach of Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.

As a result, they applied the standard five-place grid penalty for such an infraction. Inthraphuvasak will serve the drop in both the Sprint and Feature Races this weekend.

title: Stenshorne ‘feeling good’ after finishing fastest in Lusail Free Practice
excerpt:
Martinius Stenshorne was quickest in Friday’s Lusail Free Practice and he is hoping to convert this into another pole position.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was a constant in the top 10 for much of the session but late improvements put him at the top of the timesheets.

Stenshorne’s final lap of a 1:38.030 put him 0.115s ahead of TRIDENT’s John Bennett, giving him a fine start after a few weeks of preparation to be ready for the challenge of Qatar.

“To prepare for this weekend, it was all about the normal sim prep at the factory and then just some physical training,” said Stenshorne.

“I did a bit of karting as well over the break, but apart from that, not much, and it went well, building into it a bit in the beginning, but after the pit stop, we did some changes and it worked well, so a good first session.”

Stenshorne was fastest in Free Practice by over a tenth to the rest of the field

Stenshorne took his maiden Formula 2 pole position last time out in Baku, and hopes Free Practice is a sign that a second Aramco Pole Position Award could be on the cards.

“Practice went well this morning, so I don't see why it can't be possible,” said Stenshorne on taking pole.

PRACTICE: Stenshorne quickest for Rodin in Lusail opener

TITLE FIGHT FAVOURITES: What the contenders are saying ahead of Lusail

“Obviously, it's going to be very different conditions, track will be faster, car will be faster, so we'll see, but feeling good.”

While there is a lot that Stenshorne could personally gain from a strong weekend in Lusail, a key part of his focus is on helping Rodin in the Teams’ Championship.

Stenshorne is keen to help Rodin win the Teams' title over the next two rounds

The Farnham, Surrey-based team are third in the Standings and just 37 points behind leaders Campos Racing, and the Norwegian is hopeful that they can overturn this deficit.

“Obviously, we are still in the fight for the Teams championship, so we will do what we can there,” he said.

“I can also gain some points, that would be nice. Maybe it's difficult to gain some positions in the championship, but we will see what we can do. But it would be nice to be able to take the Teams’ Championship.”

title: What To Watch For: The key storylines on F2’s return to action in Lusail
excerpt:
All the key talking points going into Round 13 in Lusail

Formula 2 is back and these next few days are critical. Lusail kicks off the final two rounds of the season where we will crown the 2026 champion.

With Rafael Câmara committed to Formula 1 for the rest of the campaign, it leaves the door open for Nikola Tsolov and Alexander Dunne in what should be an epic title fight, with three other drivers still in the mix.

That all starts in Qatar this weekend, but before we hit the track, here is a rundown of all the key talking points going into Round 13.

TSOLOV AND DUNNE PREPARE FOR BATTLE

When Tsolov and Dunne left Baku, they would have believed they'd have to beat Câmara on track to win the title.

But with the Brazilian driving in Lusail and Yas Marina for the Haas Formula 1 Team instead of Invicta Racing, Tsolov has to overturn a seven-point deficit to take the lead, with Dunne 18 points behind Câmara.

Dunne and Tsolov are separated by just 11 points going to Lusail

Tsolov could clinch the title in Qatar: if he takes a lead of 39 points or more over Dunne, or any other driver, into that round, he will win it.

As for Dunne, the Irishman is just 11 points behind Tsolov and before the break was on a superb run of form – finishing on the podium in each of the last four races.

Momentum is with the Rodin Motorsport driver but his Bulgarian rival has been a force this year, so this could be a special two weeks.

Théophile Nael steps up with Campos Racing as a Red Bull Junior

Chasing the Dream Season 8, Episode 14 – Out Today

THE OUTSIDERS WITH A CHANCE

This weekend is not just about Tsolov and Dunne, as there are three other drivers who could also be crowned champion. Gabriele Minì, Dino Beganovic and Noel León all have a fighting chance.

Minì in particular is just 37 points behind Tsolov and had been one of the more consistent drivers through the first nine rounds of the season.

Minì and Beganovic are still mathematically in with a shout of winning the title

However, a difficult three rounds in Monza, Madrid and Baku, where he did not finish on the podium, saw him lose ground to his rivals. A good few days in Lusail would bring the MP Motorsport driver back into the fight.

The same goes for Beganovic and León, who are 63 and 67 points respectively behind Tsolov. This makes it difficult, but Beganovic has been on the podium in three of the last four races – including victories in the Madrid Feature and Baku Sprint Races.

León also has three wins of his own this season and will be feeling confident about his chances. It’s all to play for in Lusail.

NEW FACES IN NEW PLACES

The grid looks slightly different to the one that we had in Baku, as there will be a few debutants this weekend.

2026 Formula 3 champion Ugo Ugochukwu joins Van Amersfoort Racing for the final two rounds, while his title rival Freddie Slater replaces Câmara at Invicta.

Nicola Lacorte also graduates to F2 with PREMA Racing, replacing Sebastián Montoya, who has moved to DAMS Lucas Oil, while Roman Bilinski will drive for Hitech.

2026 Formula 3 champion Ugo Ugochukwu will make his F2 debut this weekend in Lusail

As well as that, Nico Pino will drive for AIX Racing at the final two rounds. It will be a big weekend for all.

A SPECIAL RACE IN A SPECIAL SEASON

Before Formula 2’s 10th season comes to an end, we will be reaching another milestone in Qatar.

The Lusail Sprint Race will be the 250th in the championship’s history, marking another significant milestone for F2.

130 drivers have previously raced in F2, and several of those took part in our recent documentary, F2: Where the Stars Are Made.

If you have not yet, there is still time to watch it before we hit the track this weekend and before the landmark race on Saturday evening.

title: Théophile Nael steps up with Campos Racing as a Red Bull Junior
excerpt:
Campos Racing have announced the signing of Théophile Nael for the 2027 season, with the French driver set to compete as a member of the Red Bull Junior Team.

Nael raced for the Spanish team in Formula 3 this year and finished fifth in the Drivers’ Championship with three victories and five podiums in total.

Prior to this year, Nael claimed the 2023 Spanish F4 title and also won the 2025 Macau Grand Prix.

The 19-year-old will now graduate to Formula 2 next year and is delighted to be doing so with Campos and with the support of Red Bull.

“I’m incredibly happy and proud to join the Red Bull Junior Team and continue my journey with Campos Racing as I take the next step in my career, moving up to Formula 2,” said Nael.

“A huge thank you to everyone for their trust and continued support. I’m more motivated than ever and ready to take on this exciting new challenge. Can’t wait to get started!”

Team Principal Adrián Campos also added: “We are delighted to continue working with Théophile for another season. In his first year with us, he has demonstrated tremendous talent, a great work ethic and, above all, the potential to fight for the most ambitious goals. He has enjoyed an excellent FIA Formula 3 season, showcasing his speed, consistency and great maturity on track. We are convinced that he has all the qualities needed to take on this new challenge in FIA Formula 2, and we want to continue supporting his development. It will also be a privilege to do so alongside the Red Bull Junior Team, and we are looking forward to getting started and preparing for this exciting new chapter together”.

title: Nico Pino signs with AIX Racing for the final two rounds of the season
excerpt:
AIX Racing have announced that Nico Pino will race for the team at the final two rounds of the season in Lusail and Yas Marina.

Pino brings a wealth of experience from sportscars racing in Europe, Asia and America, and finished third in the 2023 edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

The 22-year-old, who last competed in single seater racing in 2022 in the Euroformula Open Championship, will now race for AIX, replacing Cian Shields.

Speaking about his announcement, Pino was excited for the challenge of racing in Formula 2.

"The FIA Formula 2 is the final step before Formula 1,” said Pino. “Making my debut now is a great opportunity that my team and AIX have given me, and it’s a real chance to learn.

“It’s my first time in this car, racing alongside several drivers I’ve competed against at different stages of my career, so I’m really happy to be here. It’s definitely a challenge, but I don’t know a single driver at this level who isn’t looking for challenges that push them to the limit. We’ll take it step by step”

title: Ritomo Miyata reflects on his ‘amazing’ first Formula 2 win in Madrid
excerpt:
Ritomo Miyata achieved his first Formula 2 victory in the Madrid Sprint Race, and recently we caught up with him to talk through it all.

The Hitech driver converted a P2 start into a win in Saturday’s shorter race, and made it to the podium again on Sunday, going from ninth to third.

Miyata believes his good starting positions were key to his success that weekend, having qualified inside the top 10 for just the third time in the season.

“It was an amazing weekend,” reflected Miyata. “At first this year we struggled, especially with short run performance.

“But in Madrid, we finished inside the top 10 in quali, and then we won the Sprint Race, and we got back to the podium in the Feature Race, finishing P3, and that was really good.

“Actually, we have good long run performance, it’s just we lack a bit in the short run performance. So in Madrid, it was really good.”

Miyata and Hitech celebrated two podiums in Madrid

Looking more into the Sprint Race win, Miyata spoke about the keys to victory that day.

“With Madrid, the layout looked difficult to overtake on,” he explained. “So, I was trying to focus on my start, because that's the overtake opportunity. But actually my start was good, and then I overtook P1, and then I took the lead of the race.

“Then I managed our pace, but I was expecting it would be chaos because it was so easy to hit the wall, and easy to get a Safety Car. So I tried to do my best with the restarts and then we won.”

Freddie Slater to drive for Invicta Racing at the final two rounds of the season

Ugo Ugochukwu joins Van Amersfoort Racing for Lusail and Yas Marina rounds

It was already a successful weekend for Miyata and Hitech, but a great strategy call to not pit early from the Softs paid off.

The Japanese driver was sat in third when a Safety Car was called and was able to maintain the position once he made his mandatory stop, and held on to take the final spot on the podium.

“In the Feature Race, it was the same as the Sprint, we expected the Safety Car risk,” said Miyata. “Also, in the Sprint Race, a few drivers took the option tyres, so that was good information for the Feature Race.

Miyata held P3 in the Feature Race after benefitting from the Safety Car

“We tried to avoid the Safety Car risk. Also, we needed good performance before the pit stop, and actually, before the pit stop, our pace was strong. That's why we could stay on track as long as possible.

“There was a late Safety Car, so we gained some positions. So, that's what helped us finish third in the Feature Race.”

Reflecting on the weekend overall Miyata said: “It was really good because in one weekend, we had two podiums, and that is really difficult. Of course, sometimes it happens, but it's not easy.

Bilinski to Hitech, Montoya to DAMS and Lacorte to see out 2026 with PREMA

Haas confirms Rafael Câmara will complete F1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi

“For me, it was my first win in F2, and actually, it was the first podium of my career because last year I gained from some drivers getting penalties at Spa, and I was promoted to P2.

“But this time I actually got to stand on the podium for the first time. So, I didn’t imagine I could get the podium in a Feature Race.

“Also, I was starting in P9. I thought maybe a good result would be P6 or P5. But in the end, we finished P3. It's really good, and a double podium in one weekend. It's really amazing.”

title: Freddie Slater to drive for Invicta Racing at the final two rounds of the season
excerpt:
Invicta Racing have confirmed that Freddie Slater will drive for the team in Lusail and Yas Marina.

Slater, who was confirmed to be racing for the British team in the 2027 campaign, will step up early to replace Rafael Câmara at the final two rounds.

The 18-year-old steps up to F2 after a strong campaign in Formula 3, where he fought for the title until the last race, ending up second in the Standings with one victory and eight podiums in total.

Slater will now race with Invicta in the season-ending double header and he is excited to be making his debut with the team earlier than expected.

“I’m very excited to be joining Invicta Racing for the final two rounds of the 2026 Formula 2 season,” said Slater. “Making my debut in Qatar is a great way to start preparing for my rookie year, and I’m keen to integrate myself into the team as quickly as possible.

“It’s a significant step in my career and a great opportunity, so I’m keen to start making progress on track and play my part in ending what has already been a successful season for the team on a high note.”

Invicta Racing Team Principal James Robinson also added: “We’re excited to give Freddie his Formula 2 debut across the final two rounds of this season. It’s a good opportunity to begin working with him ahead of our full campaign together in 2027, and will provide valuable experience as he adapts to the car, the championship and the demands of Formula 2. Of course, this has come somewhat earlier than planned following Rafael’s move to Haas, which is thoroughly deserved and we wish him all the best. Freddie has big shoes to fill at such short notice, but we’re confident in his ability and looking forward to welcoming him as we push for a strong end to the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.”

The Director of the Audi Driver Development Programme Allan McNish added: “We are pleased to see Freddie getting the opportunity to make his Formula 2 debut earlier than expected. These final two rounds will give him important experience ahead of his first full campaign next year, allowing him to start working with Invicta Racing and getting familiar with the championship. It's another important step in his development, and one that fits well with the work we're doing together through the Audi Driver Development Programme. We're looking forward to seeing him get started and wish him and Invicta Racing all the best for these final two rounds of the season.”

title: Ugo Ugochukwu joins Van Amersfoort Racing for Lusail and Yas Marina rounds
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu is set to step up to Formula 2 for the final two rounds of the 2026 season, joining Van Amersfoort Racing.

The American driver graduates having won this year’s FIA Formula 3 title, achieving two victories and seven podiums in total.

Ugochukwu will now partner Rafael Villagómez for the Lusail and Yas Marina rounds at VAR.

Speaking about the announcement, Ugochukwu thanked the Dutch team for the opportunity and expressed excitement at the chance to jump into the F2 car.

“I’m really happy to be joining FIA Formula 2 for the final two rounds of the 2026 season. A big thank you to Van Amersfoort Racing for this opportunity. I’m looking forward to getting out on track in Qatar and Abu Dhabi and seeing everyone out there.”

Van Amersfoort Racing Team Principal Brad Joyce added: “We are very happy to welcome Ugo to the team for the final two rounds of the FIA Formula 2 season. Winning the FIA Formula 3 Championship is a fantastic achievement and a great reflection of the performances he delivered throughout the year. Ugo has had a very strong career so far with successes in several different categories. These two events will give him his first experience of Formula 2 competition. We look forward to welcoming him to the team, working together in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, and aiming to finish the season strongly over these final 2 rounds.”

title: Bilinski to Hitech, Montoya to DAMS and Lacorte to see out 2026 with PREMA
excerpt:
Three teams have confirmed driver changes for the final rounds of the 2026 FIA Formula 2 season in Lusail and Yas Marina.

Firstly, Roman Bilinski will compete with Hitech while Sebastián Montoya will move to DAMS Lucas Oil for the final rounds.

PREMA Racing has confirmed that Nicola Lacorte will step up to the Championship and see out the season with the team.

All three drivers have been confirmed for next season but will now get vital experience at their new teams ahead of next year.

Bilinski will be replacing Colton Herta at Hitech, while Montoya moves to DAMS in place of the British-Polish driver. Lacorte will arrive in F2 to take the place of the Colombian.

Speaking about joining Hitech, Bilinski said: “I'm really excited to be joining Hitech for the final two rounds of the season. Having the opportunity to work with the team ahead of 2027 is a real bonus.

“It means we can start working together straight away, get to know each other and build a strong foundation ahead of next year. Of course, I’ll be hoping for some strong results to close out the current season.”

Montoya said he was excited to begin working with DAMS: “Very happy for the opportunity to start working with DAMS! The sim and preparation was a lot of fun learning the way the team works and operates, I think it’s a very good opportunity for myself to adapt to the team dynamic and for them to see the way I work so we start with the right foot!”

Lacorte said of his joining PREMA: “I’m really happy to be returning to PREMA for the final two rounds of the Formula 2 season. It’s great to have the opportunity to race with the team for the last two 2026 races and I’ll make the most of this experience to head into next year even stronger.”

title: Haas confirms Rafael Câmara will complete F1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi
excerpt:
Haas has confirmed that Rafael Câmara will see out of the remainder of the 2026 Formula 1 season.

It means the Brazilian will race in the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix, missing the final two rounds of the FIA Formula 2 campaign.

The Brazilian debuted in F1 at his home event in Sao Paulo and competed in the Las Vegas Grand Prix this weekend.

He will be in action for the American F1 team once again in Qatar and complete the season in F1 at Yas Marina ahead of his full-time Formula 1 rookie campaign in 2027.

Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu said that Câmara's learnings had already been a positive and that the Brazilian would gain further track time ahead of his rookie season.

“We’re excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America. I’m delighted that Rafa’s embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway.”

title: Nicola Lacorte steps up with PREMA Racing for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Nicola Lacorte will step up to FIA Formula 2 with PREMA Racing in the 2027 season.

The 19-year-old graduates to F2 after two years in Formula 3, finishing the 2026 campaign 19th in the Standings with 33 points, the highlight coming at Monza where he won the Feature Race.

Lacorte previously joined forces with PREMA for the 2023 Italian F4 campaign, where he achieved one victory and a pole position.

At the announcement, Lacorte spoke of his delight at getting the chance to return to PREMA for this next chapter of his career.

“I’m really happy to be back with PREMA Racing for the 2027 Formula 2 season,” said Lacorte. “I already felt a warm welcome from Stephen and the whole team. This is an important step in my career and a challenge I’m really looking forward to. I can’t wait to get started.”

PREMA Racing Team Principal Stephan Mitas also added: “Nicola is a fast, determined young Italian driver who has shown real progression in Formula 3, and he is exactly the kind of talent PREMA is built to develop. We want to start 2027 strongly and are excited to work with Nicola to do just that.”

title: Hitech confirms Roman Bilinski for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Hitech has confirmed that Roman Bilinski will race for the team and partner Joshua Duerksen in 2027.

The Polish-British driver is currently in his rookie FIA Formula 2 campaign, with a season-best result of P2 in the Monaco Sprint Race.

Bilinski said that he was looking forward to getting started with his new team after the final rounds of the season.

“I'm really excited to be joining Hitech for 2027. The team has a fantastic record of success in Formula 2, so I'm very pleased to have this opportunity.

“I've learned a huge amount during my first season and I'm looking forward to bringing that experience to Hitech.”

Jan Sumann, Hitech's F2 Head of Race Engineering added: “We're very pleased to welcome Roman to Hitech for 2027. He's demonstrated his ability throughout his junior career, with championship success in Formula Regional and an impressive progression through Formula 3 into Formula 2.

“We've watched his development closely from the pit wall and he's shown good speed, race craft and the determination needed to progress. His experience this season will be valuable as he makes the transition into our team.

“With Roman joining Joshua for 2027, we have an exciting driver pairing and a great deal to look forward to. Our immediate priority is to make the most of the final two rounds and begin our preparations for next season."

title: Sebastián Montoya moves to DAMS Lucas Oil for the 2027 season
excerpt:
DAMS Lucas Oil have confirmed the signing of Sebastián Montoya for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

Montoya makes the switch to the French team for what will be his third season in Formula 2, having achieved four podiums across his two previous campaigns.

The Colombian driver impressed in his rookie campaign, finishing 12th in the Championship Standings after achieving three podium results - including a P3 in the Monte Carlo Feature Race.

Montoya will now move to DAMS for the 2027 campaign, and he is thankful for the opportunity to join the team.

"I’m very excited for the opportunity to join DAMS for the 2027 Formula 2 season," said Montoya. Its a team with a lot of history and a great ambition to create great racing drivers and win races. I can’t wait to hit the track and get started.”

Team Owner Charles Pic also added: "We are delighted to welcome Sebastian to DAMS Lucas Oil for the 2027 season. He has gained valuable experience in Formula 2 and shown great potential. We look forward to working together and fighting for strong results next season."

title: FP1 Roundup: Which Formula 2 drivers past and present are in action in Las Vegas?
excerpt:
Another Formula 1 round with Formula 2 drivers getting their opportunity in the car for the Free Practice 1 session. Here's a primer on who will be driving in the opening session of the Las Vegas Grand Prix this weekend.

Firstly, Dino Beganovic will be back in the Ferrari SF-26 this weekend, driving in place of Lewis Hamilton. It will mark the fourth FP1 session for the Swede in 2026.

"I've driven the track in the simulator and it's a great circuit, so I'm really looking forward to experiencing it in real life, going down the Strip and racing in the dark," Beganovic said. "It won't be an easy challenge for me as a rookie, driving this street circuit for the first time, but I'm excited to take it on."

Former F2 driver Jak Crawford will also be in action, taking over driving duties from Fernando Alonso at Aston Martin. It will be the first time the American has driven in an FP1 session on home soil.

"I'm really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the AMR26 in Las Vegas," Crawford said. "It's particularly special to be doing it in the United States, and I'm excited to get out on track in front of the American fans.

"My session in Mexico City finished earlier than planned, so it's great to have another opportunity to get behind the wheel again so soon. I'll be focused on making the most of the session and providing useful feedback to help the team prepare for the weekend."

The FP1 session is scheduled to get underway at 16:30 local time in Las Vegas.

title: 10 SEASONS OF FORMULA 2: Oscar Piastri on lessons and best moments in F2
excerpt:
2021 FIA Formula 2 Champion Oscar Piastri reflects on his time in the Championship, his title-winning campaign and his favourite moments from his time in F2.

How did F2 prepare you for your move up to F1?

"Well, I mean the biggest thing is it provides the stage to showcase your abilities to the F1 world. Being on the F1 weekends and being the step below F1, I think that's the main way it prepares you.

"In junior racing, with pit stops, there's that element and the car is the closest thing to an F1 car, and it's still a bit of a jump into F1. But I think the biggest thing is just the pressure and the stage."

What's your advice for the next generation of F2 drivers looking to make it into F1?

"I mean the same as always, just always try and keep learning. I think at that point you're still very early in your career you know? Obviously it's late in your junior career, but in the grand scheme of things it's still very early on in your development. So just keep learning and keep learning new things."

What is your favourite win, moment and overtake from your time in F2?

"I think my favourite moment is winning the Championship. Favourite win, there were a few good ones, but I think probably winning the Sprint Race in Bahrain.

"It was at the time the three Alpine Academy drivers were fighting for the win on the final lap and we went into Turn 1 three-wide. We came back through the field after a Safety Car and put new tyres on, so that was a really that was the most exciting win I've ever had. Overtake? Favourite overtake is probably the three wide moment as well."

‘My most enjoyable year’ says Maini as he reflects on positive 2026 campaign

LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of Oliver Goethe for the 2027 season

What is your favourite off-track memory from your time in F2?

"I mean, I think in general PREMA always made things fun. So, probably some of the funny media things we have to do.

You're racing in F1 as a back-to-back F2 and F3 Champion. How much pride do you get from that?

"Yeah, I mean I do have a sense of pride from that and they're always nice memories to look back on. But I think for me, especially now with a few years in F1, I always look back on the lessons that I learned in those championships rather than the results I had.

"So I think that's the biggest thing, but definitely to achieve that success is something very proud of."

title: ‘My most enjoyable year’ says Maini as he reflects on positive 2026 campaign
excerpt:
Kush Maini is having his most enjoyable Formula 2 campaign and a successful relationship with ART Grand Prix is a key reason why.

The Indian driver has one victory, two podiums in total, as well as two pole positions, and with two rounds to go, he is ninth in the Championship Standings on 90 points.

Recently Maini reflected on his season so far, from an inconsistent start to showing his and the team’s true potential in the middle portion of the year.

“It started off a bit slow,” says Maini. “Pace-wise we've always been there, but we definitely left a lot of points on the table.

“Then we had a few unlucky moments like in Miami, leading the Feature Race and then having the Safety Car come out and then the same thing happened in Budapest.

“So definitely some points left, but I think performance-wise we've shown what we can do. We've done a couple poles and been one of the fastest drivers on some of the weekends. So, team and car-wise it's been amazing.

Maini and ART have formed a great relationship this season

“It's been amazing to work with ART and it's been very consistent. The car's been consistently quick and it's definitely my most enjoyable year in F2. I'm looking forward to seeing where this momentum can take us and where we finish.”

A MUCH-NEEDED PARTNERSHIP

This is Maini’s fourth season in Formula 2, after choosing to return to the grid following a campaign where he finished 16th in the Standings with 32 points.

The Alpine Academy member joined ART after the French team’s worst statistical season in the Championship – finishing eighth with 127 points, which was their lowest return in F2.

Maini says it was a gamble for both he and the team given the last few seasons, but together they have helped each other show their best form.

LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of Oliver Goethe for the 2027 season

Rafael Câmara to race for Haas in Las Vegas Grand Prix

“I think ART have been through a few tough seasons and so have I,” he acknowledges. “So, it was a massive gamble for us both to link up, and I think it's worked out really well.

“I think it's shown that ART's potential is there and my potential is there too. We've worked really well together and we've both been so hungry to prove everyone wrong. So that hunger has really driven us to work really hard and it's brought out the best in both sides.”

Maini says he does not feel he has changed much in his driving this way

THE KEY AREA OF GROWTH IN 2026

Maini however does not believe his driving has changed all that much this year compared to his previous seasons.

While Maini acknowledges some improvements in his mental approach on race weekends, he believes his partnership with ART has given him a greater platform to show his best form.

“To be honest, I think I'm driving very similar to how I've driven every year,” he says. “Obviously, there's a few things on managing the mental side which I'm a lot better at now. I'm a lot more mature, which is definitely a positive and helps.

“But mainly the team has given me a very comfortable and a great platform to prove my best. They've trusted me after every session, even when it's not gone well. They've always bigged me up.

“They've never lied, always been honest, always been upfront with everything. So, giving that platform to a driver is very important because that makes you feel like you're at home and then you can maximise yourself.”

Maini is thankful for the support of ART and Alpine over the last season

ALPINE’S BACKING

While Maini has a lot of appreciation for the relationship with ART, he says his work with Alpine has also played a huge part in keeping his confidence high.

Maini jumped into the car for the Formula 1 team at the post-season test in Yas Marina and has since taken part in several Testing of Previous Cars Programmes (TPC) with them.

After a tough 2025 campaign, the Indian driver says these opportunities have helped him a lot. “I think Alpine has played a big part,” says Maini when asked about keeping his confidence.

What the drivers said - F2: Where F1 Stars are Made

Nikola Tsolov confirmed as Red Bull reserve driver for the 2027 Formula 1 season

“Jumping into the F1 car last year after my worst year in F2 and being on the pace straight away with the best in the world was a massive, massive confidence boost.

“That's actually something that made my mindset the way it is going into this year. Alpine has played a massive part in keeping that trust that I can do it. They have nothing to gain keeping me around unless they feel I can bring something to them.

“In all the testing, they are always very impressed, and they are always very happy. That keeps my confidence as a driver high because in this sport, once that confidence goes down, it's very tough to build it up.

The ART driver scored on his only victory of the season in Barcelona

“That's why every driver is here, to try and get to the next level. Alpine and I have worked very well together the last few years. I helped them a lot on the sim and all the TPC testing and any run plans they want to run by in those test days to help their drivers.

“I know they know that I can perform when I'm in the car. We're still waiting for me to try and get that super-licence because that's the main step. But pace-wise, driver-wise, maturity-wise, I think they have a lot of trust in me.”

ENDING ON A HIGH

Even with the upturn in form, Maini knows that the results could have been better, having missed out on Feature Race victories in Miami and Budapest.

The ART driver’s lone victory came in the Barcelona Sprint where he won by 7.2s, and while he would have loved to add more wins to tally, he feels he has showed his pace.

“In Miami, we were leading by six seconds, we had amazing pace and I think we deserved to win that,” he adds.

Maini is aiming to end the season on a high after losing out on points in a couple of Feature Races

“Obviously, there was a Safety Car and we got a bit unlucky there and we finished fifth, so that's already 15 points gone. Then Budapest, leading the Feature Race by five seconds, then the Safety Car.

“What I would say is every time we've got into the lead, we've shown our pace, and we've pulled away. In Barcelona, we won by seven seconds. It shows that we can be very dominant, it's just now the stars have got to align a bit.

“So I will just stick to my processes and have points scoring weekends every weekend and put myself in the best possible opportunity to score the most points that myself and the car can potentially do.”

title: LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of Oliver Goethe for the 2027 season
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion have confirmed their first driver signing for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season, with Oliver Goethe set to race for the team next year.

Goethe is in the midst of his second campaign in Formula 2 and has so far achieved two podiums in results in the Spielberg Feature and Monza Sprint Races.

Prior to stepping up to F2, Goethe won the 2022 Euroformula Open Championship and second in the 2024 Macau Grand Prix.

The German driver will continue in F2 for a third full season and is delighted to take on a new challenge with the newest team in the paddock.

“I’m absolutely thrilled to be joining LN4 Fusion for the 2027 season,” said Goethe. “It’s a really exciting project, and I can’t wait to be part of it. I genuinely feel that next year could be my year, and I’m determined to make the most of this opportunity. For now, my focus is on finishing this season on a high before getting straight to work preparing for 2027.

“I’m ready to give it everything I’ve got! I’m grateful to my family, the team around me, my sponsors and Motorsport Team Germany for their continued support. As part of the cooperation between Motorsport Team Germany and Audi, I have already completed several sessions in Audi’s F1 simulator, gaining useful experience and insight into the tracks ahead of the upcoming season.”

LN4 Fusion Chief Executive Officer Dan Richards also added: “I think Oliver is a great choice for our team. He knows the car, the tracks and the championship well, and his podiums this year show that he has taken the steps needed to fight at the front. We want to give him the environment and support he needs to continue making progress towards his ultimate goal, and we are confident that together we can have a strong season.”

title: Rafael Câmara to race for Haas in Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Haas has confirmed that Rafael Câmara will race for the team at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

It follows the Brazilian’s Formula 1 debut at his home event in Sao Paulo where he qualified 13th and accumulated vital race experience ahead of his rookie F1 campaign in 2027.

Câmara said that he was eager to get back in the car and continue his learning around what will be another new circuit for him.

“I’m looking forward to getting back in the car in Las Vegas. Brazil was a good learning experience, and now the focus is on building on that, improving step by step and making the most of every session. It’s a new circuit for me, so there’s a lot to learn, but I’ll do my best to keep progressing throughout the weekend.”

Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu added: “In Brazil, our 2027 recruit Rafa Câmara made his debut under extremely challenging conditions and showed us and the world why we signed him for 2027. We're looking forward to building on that for his second race weekend with us.”

title: What the drivers said - F2: Where F1 Stars are Made
excerpt:
As FIA Formula 2 celebrates 10 years of competition, F2: Where F1 Stars are Made features insights from those that have graduated from the Championship into Formula 1.

From the first champion Charles Leclerc to the drivers that have moved on from F2 and become F1 World Champion in Lando Norris and Kimi Antonelli, here are a few quotes from those that have been there and done it.

HOW FORMULA 2 PREPARED THEM FOR F1

Charles Leclerc

“Formula 2, there was the strategy as well that you start learning. I think that's where you start working with more and more people and that's very useful for Formula 1.

“Before that, you kind of race with a lot less spotlight on you, but surely you know in the back of your head now you're performing in front of the people that will decide your future.

“It's, again, a very important learning process because you've got to be performing in these kinds of situations because when you get to Formula 1, then it's 100 times that and everybody looks at every single thing you do in the car.

“To perform at this level in front of so many people for the first time in their career is actually a very important learning process for Formula 1 right after.”

Oliver Bearman

“The Formula 2 learning that I took was big. I learned a lot about myself, how I react under pressure, how I react in challenging situations, how I interact with people as well.

“I think it's a really important skill. So I think I entered Formula 2 and Formula 3 as a kid, and I came out more of an adult.”

THE BIGGEST LESSONS FROM F2

Charles Leclerc - 2017 FIA Formula 2 Champion

Kimi Antonelli

“Coming from Formula Regional was a big step, but you know, just the fact also being in the same weekend as the Formula 1, understanding a bit more the dynamics and what F2 taught me a lot is trying to be there straight away because obviously with only one practice and then straight into qualifying, and especially on new tracks, it was very important to understand where the limit was and trying to get as close as possible to then be ready for qualifying.”

Oscar Piastri

“Going through the junior ranks, all the cars are very different. You know how you had to drive the F4 car and then went to F3, it was different again. F2 was different again. So you're always kind of learning new things in some ways subconsciously.

“I think that adaptability, that's the really important thing going through the ranks because you don't have that much track time. You don't have any sets of tyres to really get in the swing of things. You've got to adapt very quickly.”

MAKING THE MOST OF THE F2 OPPORTUNITY

Oscar Piastri - 2021 FIA Formula 2 Champion

Alex Albon

“This is your chance, this is your opportunity to make that next step. You have an opportunity that no other championship has where you are really in the eyeline of all the Team Principals and so you have a good race, you need to take advantage of that.

“You cannot be shy and miss out an opportunity because you didn't go up and have a chance with various teams.

“I remember that year, I had, I think it was three pole positions in a row and that's when a conversation with Red Bull started.

“You rub shoulders all the time, you see everyone, you see the Formula 1 drivers, you see the Formula 1 Team Principals. That immediate communication with the Team Principal goes a lot further than having a conversation through a manager and I think that also helps me kind of get my case out there.”

George Russell

“There were seven drivers from that season who all raced in Formula 1. So I think that must be one of the highest, as a percentage, of drivers who ended up racing [in F1].

“Everybody's in the same car, so everybody has that same opportunity. I was racing against Lando and Alex, and so many great drivers who also made it to Formula 1 - Nyck de Vries, Nicholas Latifi.

“It's quite surreal because when you're younger, all the F1 drivers look like superheroes. Every time you see them, you're in awe. And in F2, you feel like you're within touching distance of Formula 1. When suddenly you're on the grid with them, it's just crazy.”

BECOMING A WORLD CHAMPION

Lando Norris - 2025 Formula 1 World Champion

Lando Norris

“A Formula 1 world championship is an incredible thing to achieve and hopefully [it can] inspire some of the younger kids that are in F2 now or F3 or F4 in terms of that's the correct ladder to do.

“I didn't win Formula 2 so it doesn't mean you have to win Formula 2 if you want to get into Formula 1 if you want to be a champion.

“I think that's a good thing and I think what was showcased very well in that year of F2 just how many good drivers came through it and if you want to race against the best obviously Formula 2 was certainly and still certainly is exactly that.

“To be the first F1 champion that's come through F2 is pretty special. So something that will always put a smile on my face for sure.”

You can watch the full documentary FIA Formula 2: Where F1 Stars Are Made here.

title: Nikola Tsolov confirmed as Red Bull reserve driver for the 2027 Formula 1 season
excerpt:
Nikola Tsolov will take up the role of reserve driver for both the Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls Formula 1 Team in the 2027 season.

Tsolov achieves this position off the back of a stellar 2026 first full campaign in Formula 2, where with two rounds to go in Lusail and Yas Marina he is second in the Drivers’ Championship having taken six victories.

The Bulgarian driver joined the Red Bull Junior Program in 2025, and that season finished second in the FIA Formula 3 Championship.

The 19-year-old got his first experience in a Formula 1 car in August, driving for Racing Bulls at Imola, before taking part in the opening practice session of the Mexico City Grand Prix with the team.

Red Bull has also confirmed that alongside his responsibilities as a Reserve Driver, Tsolov will also undertake an extensive development programme, combining simulator and development work with valuable track experience through Free Practice sessions, Testing of Previous Cars (TPC), selected test sessions and tyre testing.

Following the announcement, Tsolov thanked Red Bull for their support and reaffirmed his hopes of being an F1 driver.

“I’m incredibly happy and grateful to Red Bull for giving me this opportunity,” said Tsolov. “Since joining the Junior Team, I’ve received amazing support and have developed so much, both as a driver and as a person. My career has progressed incredibly quickly, and I owe a lot to everyone who has believed in me and helped me get to this point.

“My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver. Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting. I’m confident that with the Team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.

“I know there is still a lot to learn, but I’m ready to work hard, make the most of every opportunity and give everything I have to the Team. For now, my immediate focus is on finishing the F2 season as strongly as possible.”

CEO and Team Principal of Oracle Red Bull Racing Laurent Mekies also added: “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years. To fight for the Championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

"We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.

"For now, Nikola still has an important job to finish in F2. We wish him every success in the final two rounds and will be supporting him all the way as he fights for the Championship.”

title: Formula 3 Champion Ugo Ugochukwu steps up with Campos Racing in 2027
excerpt:
The 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champion Ugo Ugochukwu will step up to FIA Formula 2 with Campos Racing for next season.

Ugochukwu graduates to F2 after a stellar title-winning campaign, where he achieved two victories and seven podiums in total, while also helping Campos retain the Teams’ title.

The American driver had an exceptional 2026, as he also won the Formula Regional Oceania Trophy at the start of the year.

Ugochukwu boasts a strong resume in single seater racing having also won the 2023 Euro 4 Championship and also the 2024 Macau Grand Prix.

The 19-year-old will now graduate to Formula 2 in 2027 with Campos, and at the announcement, he expressed his delight at continuing with the team.

“Proud to announce I’ll be staying with Campos Racing for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season,” said Ugochukwu. “After winning the F3 Championship together, I’m ready to take the next step and fight for more success.”

Campos Racing Team Principal Adrián Campos also added: “Ugo is an exceptionally talented driver with enormous potential. Since we started working together, we have been able to see his ability, professionalism and, above all, his continuous improvement first-hand. He is a driver who never stops learning and getting better, and that is essential when taking the next steps in a racing career. Winning the FIA Formula 3 title in our first season together is a fantastic achievement, but so is all the work behind that success and the progress he has made throughout the year.

“We are very pleased with the relationship we have built and the way we have developed together. That is why we approach his FIA Formula 2 debut in 2027 with great optimism. We know how demanding this championship is, but we firmly believe in his talent and his ability to keep progressing. We are looking forward to continuing to support him through this new challenge and working together to help him take another important step in his career.”
